declaration.preface:
Polyventive LLC (Group) is deeply committed to upholding the highest standards of labour and human rights across its operations and supply chain. We recognize that the well-being, health, safety, and dignity of our employees, contractors, suppliers, and stakeholders are fundamental to our long-term sustainability. This Labour & Human Rights Policy reflects our commitment to global standards such as the International Labour Organization (ILO) Conventions, the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs), and the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Our aim is to foster a safe, inclusive, and supportive work environment that promotes equity, fairness, respect, and continuous growth. As part of our responsibility, we extend these standards to our suppliers and partners, ensuring that human rights are protected not only within Polyventive but also across our global value chain.
declaration.declaration: Polyventive is proud to uphold and promote labour and human rights through the following commitments:
declaration.scope: This policy is applicable across all Polyventive LLC (Group) facilities, employees, Workers, contractors, Sub-Contractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders globally, including the communities in which Polyventive operates. Polyventive ensures that labour and human rights standards are consistently maintained throughout all its sites, operations, and business relationships

focusAreas: Voluntary Labour & Prohibition of Forced and Child Labour
Freedom of Association and Collective Bargaining
Child Labour, Forced Labour & Human Trafficking
External Stakeholder Human Rights & Supply Chain

Employees Health and Safety: Comprehensive health and safety management systems include regular risk assessments, training programs, provision of appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE), and annual health check-ups for all employees. All facilities comply with local and international health and safety regulations, and potential hazards are proactively monitored and mitigated.
Compliance with Laws: Polyventive and its suppliers fully comply with all applicable U.S. federal, state, and local laws, as well as international labour, immigration, health & safety, and environmental regulations.
Voluntary Labour & Prohibition of Forced: We maintain a zero-tolerance policy against child labour, forced labour, bonded labour, or involuntary servitude, including abusive forms of prison labour. All workers must retain control over their identity documents. Employment shall be freely chosen, with respect for rest days and limits on maximum working hours under the Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) and other applicable laws.

We comply with and enforce the California Transparency in Supply Chains Act (2010) and Canada’s Fighting Against Forced and Child Labor in Supply Chains Act (S-211). All suppliers are required to certify compliance with these acts and with Polyventive’s own standards prohibiting child and forced labour.
Equal Opportunity, Non-Discrimination, a: Polyventive prohibits discrimination, harassment, or retaliation based on race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected category. We actively promote diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) as a business strength
Harassment and Abuse: Every employee shall be treated with dignity and respect. Physical, sexual, and psychological harassment or abuse is strictly prohibited. Confidential grievance mechanisms are available to all employees to report any violations without fear of retaliation.
Compensation and Benefits: Polyventive ensures fair and competitive wages, complying with at least statutory minimum wages, overtime pay, and legally mandated benefits across all operations. Compensation is regularly benchmarked to remain competitive and sustainable.
Working Hours and Overtime: Working hours are maintained in line with local laws. Overtime is voluntary, compensated at legally mandated or premium rates, and capped to prevent overwork.
Freedom of Association and Collective Ba: Polyventive respects the right of employees to join unions or other associations of their choice and to engage in collective bargaining without interference, in compliance with local and national laws.
Health, Safety, and Well-being: We are committed to providing safe, healthy, and ergonomic workplaces in compliance with OSHA and international health & safety standards. We target zero workplace incidents through continuous training, risk assessments, hazard prevention, annual health check-ups, and provision of PPE.
Supplier Responsibility and On-Site Audi: Suppliers are required to uphold Polyventive’s labour and human rights standards. To ensure compliance, Polyventive conducts quarterly supplier audits covering environmental practices, fair labour, treatment of workers, diversity, and community impacts. Non-compliance requires corrective action within agreed timelines, monitored through follow-up audits. Findings remain confidential and are used solely for improvement.
External Stakeholder Human Rights: Polyventive respects the rights of local communities, customers, and external partners. We engage stakeholders to ensure our operations support and do not infringe upon community well-being, while promoting positive social impact.
Working Conditions: Maintain 100% of employees have access to clear, two-way communication channels (e.g., suggestion boxes, digital platforms) by Year 2030.
Maintain working hours at 8 hours/day and 48 hours/week with 1 day off per week and voluntary overtime not exceeding 4 hours/week.
Maintain overtime pay at 2x basic wage, with annual wage and benefits reviews to ensure fair and competitive compensation packages.
Provide training to 100% Employees regarding working Conditions by Year 2030.
Labour Relations: Hold quarterly meetings with employee representatives to address workplace concerns and improve conditions.
Ensure all employees are free to associate and bargain collectively, with open engagement channels between management and unions or representatives.
Career Management and Development: Conduct a minimum of one upskilling workshop per quarter for corporate staff.
Child Labour, Forced Labour & Human Traf: Ensure no employment of individuals under the age of 18, with all supply chain partners fully compliant with Polyventive’s labour standards.
Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI): Conduct periodic DEI workshops, and track progress through the DEI Committee.
Harassment and Discrimination: Establish and maintain a confidential grievance mechanism for reporting discrimination and harassment, accessible to all employees.
Ensure all complaints are addressed and resolved within 14 working days, with proper documentation and follow-up.
Conduct anonymous workplace culture surveys annually to monitor inclusivity and respect in the work environment.
Grievance Redressal and Social Protectio: Maintain a 24x7 anonymous grievance reporting platform, with structured escalation through HR and grievance cells.
External Stakeholder Human Rights & Supp: Participate in a minimum of 1 multi-stakeholder or industry-led human rights initiatives per year.

policy.monitoring:
Employee Feedback Surveys: Regular surveys are conducted to assess employee satisfaction with working conditions, safety, and career development.

Health and Safety Audits: Polyventive conducts regular health and safety audits at all facilities to identify risks and take corrective actions promptly.

Risk Assessment: Comprehensive risk assessments are carried out periodically to proactively identify potential hazards in the workplace, evaluate their impact, and implement appropriate mitigation strategies.

Polyventive’s Labour & Human Rights Policy is publicly accessible and communicated internally to ensure all employees and stakeholders are informed.

Employees and external stakeholders are encouraged to report any violations or concerns through confidential reporting channels without fear of retaliation.

Audit Integration: All practices and KPIs are reviewed through internal assessments and third-party evaluations such as Together for Sustainability (TFS) audits.

Feedback Loops: Employee and stakeholder feedback will be used to identify new opportunities for improvement.

Stakeholder Dialogue: Polyventive will actively engage in dialogue with communities, clients, and other key stakeholders to ensure shared responsibility in upholding labour and human rights.
policy.reviewMechanism:
Polyventive is committed to ensuring the continued accuracy, relevance, and transparency of its Labour & Human Rights Policy and reporting practices.

Annual Review Protocol: The policy and associated reports will be reviewed annually by a cross-functional team, with inputs from employees, partners, and external stakeholders.

Benchmarking: Polyventive will continuously reassess its practices against evolving global labour and human rights standards (e.g., UN SDGs, ILO conventions, SASB guidelines).

Commitment to Zero Incidents: Polyventive aims to maintain zero incidents related to workplace discrimination, harassment, and safety failures.

The Labour & Human Rights Policy will be reviewed annually by the Human Resources Director for its effectiveness, and relevance. This review will ensure that the policy adapts to changing regulations, stakeholder feedback, and evolving company goals. Updates and changes will be communicated to all employees and stakeholders as necessary.
